I address the cameras from 10.0.0.2 on up, Why that scheme? not many people use 10.0.0.x, and it's the least typing for an IP. handy when sometimes all you have to type with is a mouse.

I think your biggest expense will be the cameras themselves, really. Any ONVIF compliant camera should be sufficient, but in a lot of ways you tend to get what you pay for, in cameras. I like the Samsung WiseNet cameras, though you have to turn the motion detection on in the camera's control panel for it to work. I like the hikvision cameras, but their framerate could be better. beautiful view angle and quality though. I bought some of their 4mp domes for myself. At ~$100-150 a camera, that's still $800-1200 worth for 8 cameras.

Beyond that, I suppose it depends on your use case too. What you're trying to see, how high a resolution you need.
